record.tranche_reason: The post reports interpretability experiments on Whisper, including polysemantic acoustic neurons, but does not test superposition, capacity pressure, feature geometry, or why neurons are polysemantic.
record.gate_note: The post reports two encoder MLP neurons with polysemantic behavior across activation ranges; recorded as related findings, not as tests of whether capacity pressure caused that behavior. Attention-window and embedding-substitution experiments concern localization and transcription, not the claim versions. No values from plots are available in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The post interprets Whisper tiny with max-activating examples, SAEs, attention masking and embedding substitution. It reports polysemantic neurons and interpretable SAE features only qualitatively. It does not test capacity pressure, toy-model geometry, SAE feature canonicity or feature dimensionality, and the model is an audio-text model rather than an LLM.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author concludes that Whisper's encoder has human-interpretable (listenable) acoustic features and highly localized attention, and that the decoder alone acts as a weak LM. The work is a first, non-comprehensive step, with possible dataset bias from using dataset examples.
record.recipe_differences: The post does not apply or compare the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The author reports that earlier encoder layers 0 and 1 did not yield listenable features, while simple probes on layers 2 and 3 suggested language-related features; per-head attention localization also varied.

fits_no_version.finding: Two Whisper encoder MLP neurons respond to different sounds at different activation ranges.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Acoustic-model neurons can be polysemantic across activation ranges; the cause is not established.

fits_no_version.finding: SAEs trained on the Whisper encoder residual stream yield features the author calls highly interpretable, often phonemes. Most of the first 50 neurons in blocks.2.mlp.1 map to a single phoneme label, and several are N/A.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dictionary learning recovers interpretable phoneme-like features in an audio transformer (qualitative, no metrics).

record.problems: Feature examples were selected from dataset examples rather than an optimization-based visualization method, which the author notes could bias the features toward the dataset. The post describes the work as non-comprehensive; polysemanticity examples are qualitative, and the supplied text does not include the referenced plots or audio details.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were included because they concern attention localization, transcription, or decoder language modeling rather than the claim versions.

untested.parts: All parts: no toy models, sparsity sweep or geometry.
All parts: polysemanticity is observed, but no capacity or importance analysis is done.
All parts: the cause of the polysemanticity is not examined.
SAE features on the residual stream are only called 'highly interpretable', with no metrics. The model is Whisper (audio), not an LLM.
All parts: no completeness, stability or canonicity tests.

record.verdict_notes: The SAE residual-stream result (Section 1.2) is the nearest thing to V4. It is qualitative, comes from an audio-text model and has no numbers, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test. If V4 is widened to non-LLM transformers, it could be added as a T3 row with cannot_determine strength.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether feature competition for capacity explains polysemanticity or assigns dedicated dimensions to important features.
Whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure, and whether it is insufficient evidence of superposition.
Whether LLM features are spread across neurons or sparse features are recoverable by a dictionary; the studied model is Whisper.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.
